technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot 3.x (Java 17+ baseline) as the foundation for the new Boot-based ModuleRunner (U4), replacing the legacy xd-container runtime.
Reuse the existing gpfdist sink module by extracting the protocol-handling layer into a reusable gpfdist-writer component that can be consumed by a batch job (U6).

Add three new REST endpoints following the existing Spring MVC controller patterns and conventions for the metrics module; introduce a bulk-retrieval service method that delegates to the existing per-name metric repositories to avoid duplication (U3).

Externalize the Sqoop metastore configuration through a new property (e.g., 'sqoop.metastore.config') backed by Spring property placeholders, preserving the default behavior for backward compatibility (U1).

Leverage Spring Security abstractions and GemFire's native security APIs to implement authentication/authorization for the GemFire source module; expose properties for credentials and security configuration (U5).

Restructure the test infrastructure to separate 'mock-only' test slices from 'real-repository' integration tests using Spring's @TestConfiguration, profile-based bean loading, and dedicated test source sets (U7).
Move the reactor-based data processor module from the spring-xd-modules repository into the core, adding it as a default module and removing the external dependency for processor authors (U8).
Maintain backward compatibility with existing module definitions, batch jobs, and REST clients throughout all changes.
Update reference documentation (AsciiDoc) and configuration metadata for every user-visible change.
assumptions: A single senior Java/Spring developer familiar with the Spring XD codebase is performing all the work; no onboarding ramp-up time is included.
The Spring XD codebase, build system (Gradle), and CI pipeline are already in place and do not require new infrastructure setup.
Target runtime is Java 17 or later (consistent with Spring Framework 6.0 / Spring Boot 3.x requirements).
External systems referenced in the user stories (Sqoop, HDFS, GemFire, HAWQ/GPDB, gpfdist) are available in development/test environments; effort for provisioning them is not included.

For U4 ('Scope: *'), the scope is interpreted as applying to the entire increment (i.e., U4 is a major architectural change that affects the overall delivery, not that all other user stories are out of scope).
Documentation uses the existing AsciiDoc format already present in the project; no new documentation tooling is required.
Bug fixing is estimated as a separate cross-cutting activity (approximately 10% of development effort) and is not double-counted in individual user stories.
Existing tests are green at the start of the increment; effort for fixing pre-existing failures is not included.
Effort estimates represent productive development hours (coding, testing, reviewing, documenting) and exclude meetings, administrative overhead, and waiting time.
